Q. 141. What are the duties required in the eighth commandment?

A. The duties required in the eighth commandment are, truth, faithfulness, and justice in contracts and commerce between man and man; rendering to every one his due; restitution of goods unlawfully detained from the right owners thereof; giving and lending freely, according to our abilities, and the necessities of others; moderation of our judgments, wills, and affections concerning worldly goods; a provident care and study to get, keep, use, and dispose these things which are necessary and convenient for the sustentation of our nature, and suitable to our condition; a lawful calling, and diligence in it; frugality; avoiding unnecessary lawsuits, and suretiship, or other like engagements; and an endeavor, by all just and lawful means, to procure, preserve, and further the wealth and outward estate of others, as well as our own.

metadata.synopsis: On a BCO 41 reference, the SJC tried a minister on seven charges arising from allegations of sexual misconduct, bullying, dishonesty, a civil defamation suit, contumacy, doctrinal error, and lack of fitness. It found him not guilty on every charge because the prosecution failed to meet its burden, removed all censures and administrative suspensions, and restored him to good standing. For the lawsuit charge, it rejected a categorical ban on civil suits between Christians and required proof that this suit was sinful.

metadata.synopsis: A church member appealed Presbytery’s affirmance of his conviction and excommunication for failing to heed Session admonition and membership vows, including prolonged absence from that church. The SJC affirmed and denied the appeal, holding that all four specifications—lack of reasonable indulgence, haste, prejudice, and injustice—were nonspecific and unsupported. It emphasized his admissions that the charges were true, the adequate timeline, and the bar on considering evidence not offered at trial. A dissent disputed his PCA membership, standing, and the Session’s jurisdiction.

metadata.synopsis: In a BCO 40-5 matter, the SJC held that a presbytery erred in upholding a session's erasure of a member who pled not guilty to failing to submit and pursued divorce. The session wrongly equated declining divorce counsel with refusing submission, failed to assess membership duties in another branch, failed to notify her of erasure, and proceeded without process after dropping charges. The SJC sustained the challenge, directed the session to note the notice failure and remove her under BCO 38-3(a), but ordered no express reversal.
